reason: Split by rule (quantity < 1, negative unit price), each with the ticket's reproduction value, the just-outside and just-inside boundaries and a multi-line case where only the second line is invalid, plus one regression case for the ticket's valid draft; all functional because drafts are never saved.

items.title: A valid draft is answered with 200 and the computed draft
covers: What should happen: valid drafts are answered as before
What happens step 2: quantity 2, unit price 10 -> 200, 2 units, total 20
items.reason: The fix adds validation in front of `Mediator.Send`; the ticket requires valid drafts to be answered as before (step 2: 2 units at 10 -> total 20). A regression here would break checkout for every buyer. Functional is the cheapest layer that runs the real endpoint and handler; no order is saved, so the Ordering functional host limitation does not apply.

items.title: A draft line with quantity 0 is answered with 400 problem details naming the quantity
covers: What happens step 3: quantity 0 -> 500 with empty body
What should happen: quantity below 1 is a 4xx that says what is wrong
items.reason: This is the exact reproduction in the ticket (quantity 0 gave an empty 500) and 0 is the value just outside the lower limit of 1. Functional exercises the real endpoint pipeline and proves the domain exception no longer escapes as a server error.

items.title: A draft line with quantity -2 is answered with 400 problem details naming the quantity
covers: What should happen: quantity below 1 is a 4xx that says what is wrong
items.reason: The ticket names quantity -2 as a separate failing input; a check written as `== 0` instead of `< 1` would still let negative quantities reach the domain and answer 500. Separate from TC-BUG-56-02 because it guards the negative range, not the boundary.

items.title: A draft line with quantity 1 is accepted with 200
covers: What should happen: quantity below 1 is rejected (boundary just inside: 1 is accepted)
Valid drafts are answered as before
items.reason: The limit is "below 1", so 1 is the value just inside it; an off-by-one check (`<= 1`) would wrongly reject single-unit drafts, the most common basket line. Functional, same endpoint as the rejection cases.

items.title: A draft line with unit price -5 and quantity 1 is answered with 400 problem details naming the price
covers: What happens: unit price -5 with quantity 1 -> 500
What should happen: negative price is a 4xx that says what is wrong
items.reason: The ticket's third reproduction: a negative price with a valid quantity, so only the price rule can reject it. Without it, `OrderItem` throws `OrderingDomainException` and the caller sees an empty 500.

items.title: A draft line with unit price -0.01 is answered with 400 problem details naming the price
covers: What should happen: negative price is rejected (boundary just outside: -0.01)
items.reason: -0.01 is the smallest negative money amount, just outside the "not negative" limit; it catches a check that truncates or rounds the decimal price (for example comparing `(int)UnitPrice < 0`).

items.title: A draft line with unit price 0 is accepted with 200 and total 0
covers: What should happen: only a negative price is rejected (boundary just inside: 0 is accepted)
Valid drafts are answered as before
items.reason: The rule forbids negative prices only, so 0 (a free item) is valid; a check written as `<= 0` would wrongly reject it. This is the just-inside boundary paired with TC-BUG-56-06.

items.title: A draft whose second line has quantity 0 is rejected with 400 even though its first line is valid
covers: What should happen: a draft request whose lines have a quantity below 1 (any line, not only the first)
items.reason: The ticket speaks of a request "whose lines" are invalid; real baskets have several lines and a check that only looks at the first line would let the bad one through to the domain and answer 500. Functional, same endpoint.

items.title: A draft whose second line has a negative unit price is rejected with 400 even though its first line is valid
covers: What should happen: a draft request whose lines have a negative price (any line, not only the first)
items.reason: Same multi-line risk as TC-BUG-56-08 for the price rule: the price check must inspect every line, not only the first.
